verses.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਮਿਠਾ ਬੋਲਣਾ ਜੋ ਬੋਲੈ ਸੋਈ ਜਪੁ ਜਾਪੈ।
verses.translit_en: gurmukh miThaa bolanaa jo bolai soiee jap jaapai|

en.bdb: The polite language of a Sikh brings out what he thinks in his mind and heart.

verses.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਅਖੀ ਦੇਖਣਾ ਬ੍ਰਹਮ ਧਿਆਨੁ ਧਰੈ ਆਪੁ ਆਪੈ।
verses.translit_en: gurmukh akhee dhekhanaa braham dhiaan dharai aap aapai|

en.bdb: A Sikh beholds God everywhere with his own eyes, and that is equal to a yogi's meditation.

verses.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਸੁਨਣਾ ਸੁਰਤਿ ਕਰਿ ਪੰਚ ਸਬਦੁ ਗੁਰ ਸਬਦਿ ਅਲਾਪੈ।
verses.translit_en: gurmukh sunanaa surat kar pa(n)ch sabadh gur sabadh alaapai|

en.bdb: When a Sikh listens attentively to, or himself  sings, the word of God, that is equal to the five ecstatic sounds in the brain of a yogi.

verses.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਕਿਰਤਿ ਕਮਾਵਣੀ ਨਮਸਕਾਰੁ ਡੰਡਉਤਿ ਸਿਞਾਪੈ।
verses.translit_en: gurmukh kirat kamaavanee namasakaar dda(n)ddaut sin(j)aapai|

en.bdb: Earning livelihood with his hands by a Sikh is equal to the obeisance and prostration (of Hindus).

verses.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਮਾਰਗਿ ਚਲਣਾ ਪਰਦਖਣਾ ਪੂਰਨ ਪਰਤਾਪੈ।
verses.translit_en: gurmukh maarag chalanaa paradhakhanaa pooran parataapai|

en.bdb: When, the gurmukh, walks to behold the Guru, that is equal to an extremely holy circumambulation.

verses.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਖਾਣਾ ਪੈਨਣਾ ਜੋਗ ਭੋਗ ਸੰਜੋਗ ਪਛਾਪੈ।
verses.translit_en: gurmukh khaanaa painanaa jog bhog sa(n)jog pachhaapai|

en.bdb: When the Guru oriented person eats and clothes himself, that is equal to the performance of Hindu sacrifice and offering.

verses.gurmukhi: ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਸਵਣੁ ਸਮਾਧਿ ਹੈ ਆਪੇ ਆਪਿ ਨ ਥਾਪਿ ਉਥਾਪੈ।
verses.translit_en: gurmukh savan samaadh hai aape aap na thaap uthaapai|

en.bdb: When gurmukh sleeps, that is equal to a yogi's trance and the gurmukh withdraws not his  thoughts from the object (God the Guru) of his concentration.

verses.gurmukhi: ਘਰਬਾਰੀ ਜੀਵਨ ਮੁਕਤਿ ਲਹਿਰ ਨ ਭਵਜਲ ਭਉ ਨ ਬਿਆਪੈ।
verses.translit_en: gharabaaree jeevan mukat lahir na bhavajal bhau na biaapai|

en.bdb: The householder is liberated in life; he is not afraid of the waves of the world's ocean and fear does not enter his heart.
He goes beyond the region of blessings and curses, and does not utter them.
